e.etymology: A compound of Mae and Bell, close in sound to Mabel and often a respelling of it.
A Japanese girls' name ending in ko, child. The first part depends on the kanji: elegant, correct and flourishing are common readings. Empress Masako of Japan bears the name.
A Finnish name of debated origin, usually linked with Heino, a German short form of Heinrich (Henry). Finnish immigrants brought it to Michigan and Minnesota.
A compound of Jenny and Lee. Its use in the early 1980s followed the actress Jenilee Harrison of Three's Company and Dallas.
A Japanese boys' name whose meaning depends on the kanji; common spellings join hide, excellent, with o, man or husband, and one spelling is the word for hero.
namesakes: Hideo Nomo (Dodgers pitcher, 1995 National League Rookie of the Year)
Hideo Kojima (video game designer behind Metal Gear Solid)

e.etymology: A pet form of Theodosia, by way of Docia or Doshia. Theodosia comes from Greek theos, god, and dosis, giving.
Nora with the Spanish diminutive ending -ita, in the pattern of Juanita and Anita.
A Japanese girls' name ending in ko, child. The first part depends on the kanji: clever, talented and year are common readings.
A phonetic spelling of Sade, short for the Yoruba name Folasade, honor confers a crown. It appeared in the mid-1980s with the hits of the Nigerian-born British singer Sade.

assoc.t: Sade, the singer, whose name is said this way

e.etymology: A spelling of Matt, the short form of Matthew, from Hebrew Mattityahu, gift of Yahweh.
From Old Norse Ingibjorg, which joins the name of the god Ing with bjorg, help or protection. Queens and princesses of Denmark, Norway and Sweden have borne it since the Middle Ages.
An English surname of Norman origin, from Gournay-en-Bray in Normandy.
e.note: A gurney is also a wheeled hospital stretcher.

e.etymology: A pet form of Sophronia, from Greek sophron, sensible or self-controlled.
The double name Betty Jane written as one word. Betty is a pet form of Elizabeth and Jane a feminine form of John; run-together double names were common in the 1920s.
The French form of Odilia, from the Germanic root od, wealth. Saint Odile is the patron of Alsace, and Odile is the black swan of Tchaikovsky's Swan Lake.

assoc.t: Odile, the black swan of Swan Lake

e.etymology: The Latin form of Slavic Stanislav, from stani, to stand or become, and slava, glory. Saint Stanislaus, an 11th-century bishop of Krakow, is a patron saint of Poland.
A respelling of Ethel, from Old English aethel, noble, first a short form of names such as Etheldreda and Ethelinda.

e.meaning: row of houses by a wood
e.etymology: A spelling of Woodrow, an English surname for someone who lived in a row of houses by a wood. Its 1918 peak reflects President Woodrow Wilson.
A short form of Cecilia or Cecile, from the Roman family name Caecilius, traditionally linked to Latin caecus, blind. Saint Cecilia is the patron of music.
A spelling of Nannie, an old pet form of Ann and Nancy, which go back to Hebrew Hannah, grace or favor.
A Norwegian boys' name formed as a masculine counterpart to Selma, carried to the upper Midwest by Norwegian immigrants.
A phonetic spelling of Docia, the short form of Theodosia, from Greek theos, god, and dosis, giving.
An English surname from a medieval form of Hubert, Germanic hug, mind or heart, and beraht, bright.

assoc.t: Old Mother Hubbard of the nursery rhyme

e.etymology: A spelling of Clyde, from the River Clyde that runs through Glasgow. It was a Scottish surname before it became a given name in 19th-century America.
A Scottish and Irish surname from Gaelic Mac Gille Mhoire, son of the servant of the Virgin Mary.

assoc.t: Happy Gilmore, Adam Sandler's hockey-player golfer

e.etymology: The English name of the Roman poet Publius Ovidius Naso, author of the Metamorphoses. Americans used it for boys in the 19th century, when classical names were in fashion.

assoc.t: Ovid, Roman poet of the Metamorphoses

e.etymology: A Japanese boys' name whose meaning depends on the kanji; common spellings join toshi, talented, quick or year, with o, man or husband.
